title: Water Shutoff Notice
text:
Subject: Water will be off on Thursday

Dear residents,

The city will repair a main pipe near Oak Street this week. Because of this work, the water in our building will be turned off on Thursday, March 12, from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Hot and cold water will both be unavailable during this time.

We suggest that you fill a few bottles with drinking water on Wednesday night. You may also want to take a shower before 9:00 a.m. on Thursday. The kitchen on the first floor will stay closed until the water returns.

If the repair finishes early, we will send a text message to every resident. If you have a medical need for water during the day, please call the front office at 555-0142 by Wednesday afternoon, and we will bring you bottled water.

Thank you for your patience.

Mr. Alvarez
Building Manager

explanation: The email says the water 'will be turned off on Thursday' for a few hours because of pipe repairs, so its purpose is to warn residents. It does not ask for money or explain how to report a broken pipe.

text:

title: Using Your Electric Kettle
text:
Before first use

Fill the kettle with water to the MAX line and boil it once. Pour the water away. Do this two times to clean the inside.

Daily use

1. Open the lid and fill the kettle with fresh water. Never fill it above the MAX line or below the MIN line.
2. Close the lid until it clicks.
3. Place the kettle on its base and press the switch. The blue light turns on.
4. The kettle turns off by itself when the water boils. Wait a few seconds before you pour.

Care

If white marks appear inside the kettle, pour in a cup of white vinegar and a cup of water, boil it, and leave it for 20 minutes. Then rinse well. Always unplug the kettle before cleaning. Do not put the kettle or its base in water.

If the kettle does not work, check that the plug is in the wall and that the lid is closed properly.

options: Soak it in vinegar for twenty minutes
Fill it above the MAX line and wait
Wash the kettle and its base in water

explanation: 'Before first use' says to boil water to the MAX line, pour it away, and 'do this two times.' Vinegar is only for white marks, and the base must never go in water.

options: The kettle switches itself off

explanation: Step 4 says 'The kettle turns off by itself when the water boils.' Nothing is said about the lid opening or a flashing light.

heat until it is very hot
wash with clean water
leave in a cool, dark place
explanation: After the vinegar and water are boiled and left for 20 minutes, the user should 'rinse well' to remove them. This means washing the inside with clean water.

title: New Parking Rules
text:
Subject: Parking changes at Maple Court

Hello everyone,

Starting on the first of next month, there will be some changes to parking at Maple Court. First, each apartment will receive one free parking space. title: Quiet Hours in Pine Hall
text:
Notice to Residents of Pine Hall: Quiet Hours

Starting this Monday, the residence office will begin to enforce new quiet hours. Many students have told us that noise at night makes it hard to sleep and study, especially during exam periods.

From Sunday to Thursday, quiet hours are from 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. On Friday and Saturday, they are from midnight to 9:00 a.m. During these hours, please keep music, voices, and video games low enough that they cannot be heard in the hallway. title: How CampusCycle Works
text:
CampusCycle is the university's bike-share program, designed to help students and staff travel quickly between buildings and nearby neighborhoods.

Getting started: Download the CampusCycle app and register with your university email. The first 30 minutes of every ride are free; after that, you will be charged 10 cents per minute. A refundable deposit of $20 is held on your account until you close it.

Renting a bike: Use the app's map to find a station with available bikes. Scan the code on the handlebars to unlock a bike. Adjust the seat before you ride. Helmets are not provided but are strongly recommended.

Returning a bike: Lock the bike at any station. If the station is full, the app will show you the nearest one with free space and give you an extra 15 free minutes. Bikes left outside stations can cost you a $25 fee.

If a bike is broken, tap 'Report a problem' and take a photo. You will not be charged for the ride. Bikes are checked every night.

title: Revised Grade Appeal Procedure
text:
Notice: Revised Procedure for Grade Appeals

Effective with the fall semester, the process by which students may contest a final course grade has been revised in order to ensure greater consistency across departments. Previously, a student who believed a grade to be unjust would approach the instructor informally and, if dissatisfied, write directly to the dean. Under the new procedure, a student must first submit a written request to the instructor within ten working days of the grades being posted, stating specifically which element of the assessment is disputed and why.

If the instructor does not reply within five working days or if the student remains unconvinced, the matter may be referred to a committee of three faculty members from outside the course. The committee's decision is final, save in cases where a procedural irregularity can be demonstrated. Students are encouraged to consult the Ombudsperson's office before filing, since it can offer confidential advice at no cost.

To give each instructor the final word in disputes
To discourage students from questioning their results
To make appeals more consistent across departments
explanation: The notice says the process 'has been revised in order to ensure greater consistency across departments.' The new steps do not make raising grades easier, and instructors do not have the final say.

Sending the request within five working days of grades
explanation: A student must state 'specifically which element of the assessment is disputed and why.' The request is due within ten working days; five days is the instructor's time to reply. Seeing the Ombudsperson is only encouraged.

explanation: The committee's decision is final, 'save in cases where a procedural irregularity can be demonstrated,' meaning the only exception is a procedural irregularity.

title: Global Scholars Fellowship
text:
Global Scholars Fellowship: Call for Applications

The Global Scholars Fellowship supports early-career researchers whose work crosses national or disciplinary boundaries. Each year, up to eight fellows receive a stipend of $24,000 and funding of up to $6,000 for travel and materials. Fellowships run for ten months, during which fellows are expected to be in residence at a host institution abroad for at least six.

While publications are valued, the selection committee places particular weight on the clarity and originality of the research proposal, and on evidence that the applicant has thought critically about the choice of host institution. Proposals that merely extend a doctoral thesis without a distinct question are rarely successful. Candidates should have completed their doctorate within the past four years.

Applicants must submit a 1,500-word proposal, two letters of reference, and a letter of invitation from the host. Because invitations can take weeks to arrange, applicants are advised to approach prospective hosts early. Incomplete applications will not be considered, and no extensions are granted.
